approach: Narrative literature review conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, and Web of Science (1998–2026). The authors screened titles/abstracts for studies aligned with the microbiota-metabolite-immune axis in TNBC, incorporating relevant broader breast cancer studies due to limited TNBC-specific data. Special emphasis was placed on contamination control in low-biomass tumor microbiome studies. The synthesis integrates clinical cohorts, preclinical models, and preliminary author data to stratify evidence and discuss mechanistic pathways.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive synthesis of the microbiota-metabolite-immune axis in TNBC, distinguishing between gut-derived systemic effects and intratumoral local effects. It offers a detailed catalog of metabolites (SCFAs, indoles, bile acids, toxins) and their proposed mechanisms, along with a critical evaluation of methodological limitations in low-biomass research.
contribution_and_limits.limits: The review is narrative and not systematic; it acknowledges that most evidence is extrapolated from other cancers or unstratified BC cohorts. Direct causal evidence in TNBC is scarce, and many findings are associative or preclinical. The review does not provide new experimental data but synthesizes existing fragmented evidence.

key_findings.conditions: Preclinical murine models and some clinical cohorts
key_findings.finding: Akkermansia muciniphila enrichment correlates with better chemotherapy/ICI response via M1 macrophage polarization and CD8+ T-cell activation; conversely, Lactobacillus supplementation in some models promoted M2 polarization and tumor progression.

Microbial metabolites like Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) and Indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) are associated with improved ICI responses through mechanisms involving ER stress, pyroptosis, and cytotoxic T-cell activity.

Intratumoral microbiome signals are highly susceptible to contamination artifacts; causality remains uncertain, and interpretation is limited by technical biases in sequencing and bioinformatics pipelines.

Higher baseline alpha-diversity and specific taxa (e.g., Bacteroides eggerthii, Bifidobacterium longum) are associated with pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy, while dysbiosis correlates with poor outcomes.

problem_or_question: To identify extrinsic, modifiable determinants of antitumor immunity in TNBC, specifically addressing primary and acquired resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors by elucidating the role of microbiota and microbial metabolites in shaping systemic and intratumoral immune tone.
research_scope: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), focusing on the interaction between gut and tumor-associated microbiota, microbial metabolites, and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy.
work_summary: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on how the microbiota-metabolite axis modulates antitumor immunity and response to chemoimmunotherapy in TNBC. It covers TNBC immunobiology, mammary and gut microbiome alterations, mechanistic pathways of microbial metabolites (including SCFAs, indoles, bile acids, and toxins), methodological challenges in low-biomass studies, and translational strategies such as probiotics, diet, FMT, and postbiotic approaches. The review emphasizes that while intratumoral effects are proposed, most clinically actionable evidence supports systemic gut-derived metabolites shaping the TNBC tumor microenvironment.
